sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for segment reading
sections.what: Brings in React, the router tools, the segment rules, and the industry context hook.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are needed to read the address and apply the segment rules.

sections.name: useSegment
sections.title: Reading the chosen segment
sections.what: Reads the segment from the address and returns it only if it is a valid top-level segment for an industry with a chooser. It also produces the sub-industry list for that segment and a way to clear the choice.
sections.why: The comment says URL states should always match what the chooser can show.
sections.watch_out: Segments not on the top-level list are ignored, so a deep link to a leaf segment loses its filter.

sections.name: withSegment
sections.title: Adding the segment to a link
sections.what: Appends the chosen segment to a web address so the filter follows the user to the next page.
sections.why: Keeps the segment choice while the user moves around an industry.
sections.watch_out: If the link already contains a question mark, the code adds the segment with an ampersand, so both forms must stay correct.

summary: Reads the segment filter from the address for industries that offer a segment chooser, and returns the matching list of sub-industries.
purpose: Lets an industry page be narrowed to one segment, such as one group of sub-industries, and keeps that choice while the user moves between pages.
why: The comment says only chooser-enabled industries honor the segment, so other industries behave exactly as before.
how: Finds the current industry, checks whether it has a segment chooser, and reads the segment from the address. It keeps the segment only if it is a known top-level segment. It then expands the segment into the list of sub-industries. A helper adds the segment to outgoing links, and a clear function removes it.
inputs: The current address, the industry context hook, and the segment rules in shared segments.
outputs: The industry slug, whether segments are enabled, the chosen segment, a comma-joined sub-industry list, and a clear function. A helper returns a link with the segment appended.
risks: When no industry is open, the code assumes nuclear. Unknown segment names are dropped silently.
debug: If segment filtering does nothing, check that the industry has its chooser enabled and that the segment name matches the list exactly. Check the sub-industry list passed to the projects request.
